judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not flag the 'winner-take-all' vs 'winner-loser' description of CentNN's update rule anywhere in the report. The CentNN citation and its methodology description go unchallenged.

The review discusses missing comparisons to SOM/neural gas and broader prior work, but it does not specifically challenge the claim that CentNN is updated through 'winner-take-all dynamics' against the cited Park 2000 source. No explicit contradiction or mischaracterization of that cited method is identified.

The reviewer discusses the CentNN algorithm extensively but focuses on the 'entropy proxy' terminology and performance, never mentioning the 'winner-take-all' versus 'winner-loser' methodological drift or challenging the description against the cited source (Park 2000).

The reviewer never flags the 'winner-take-all dynamics' description in the Introduction as contradicting the cited CentNN method or the paper's own winner-loser update rule. The reviewer's comments about CentNN's learning dynamics do not specifically challenge this methodological drift in the citation claim.

The reviewer mentions runtime speedups and notes single-run concerns, but never challenges the specific 6.25% figure or the arithmetic relationship between 8.344s, 7.924s, and the stated speedup percentage.

Although the reviewer says the image-data gains are '~5%' and notes some table-layout confusion, they do not specifically flag the MNIST arithmetic inconsistency between 8.344s, 7.924s, and a claimed 6.25% speed-up. They neither quote the discrepant value nor challenge the calculation directly.

The reviewer mentions the ~5% speedup on MNIST in both the summary and Major Comment 5, but they simply restate the figure as provided in the text without identifying the arithmetic inconsistency between the runtimes (8.344s to 7.924s) and the claimed 6.25% speed-up.
The reviewer does not mention any issue with the centroid initialization formula or the missing 1/n normalisation prefactor in the global mean definition.

The report raises issues with Eq. (5) and other algorithmic details, but it does not mention the Section II.C display defining the sample mean or the missing 1/n normalization factor. There is no flag corresponding to the corrupted mean formula.
The reviewer comments on Equation 5 and Equation 7, but makes no mention of the initialization formulas in Section II.C or the missing 1/n normalization prefactor in the global mean calculation.
The reviewer recommends 'a careful editorial pass' for language but does not specifically flag the word repetition 'of of' in the Introduction.

The reviewer notes occasional imprecise phrasing and recommends an editorial pass, but does not specifically identify the duplicated word 'of of' in the Introduction. Under the specific-match rule, this is not enough to count as detection.
The reviewer suggests a 'careful editorial pass' for imprecise phrasing, but does not identify the specific 'of of' word repetition in the introduction.
